proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{frontier}}\), determine explicit rate functions \(\rho_{\mathrm{est}}(N,K)\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{len}}(N,K)\) on the residual class of legal arrays satisfying
\[
\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{K_N}{N^{q_d}}=0,
\]
such that \(R_d(N,K)\asymp\rho_{\mathrm{est}}(N,K)\) and \(E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\asymp\rho_{\mathrm{len}}(N,K)\) along every such array, including exact fixed-\(K\) logarithms and every transition. This residual class includes regular arrays with \(K=o(N^{q_d})\) and irregular arrays. On every subsequence on which \(K_N/N^{q_d}\) is bounded below by a positive constant, Theorems~\texttt{thm:dimension-dependent-root-n-frontier} and~\texttt{thm:plugin-honest-length} already give the rate \(N^{-1/2}\); therefore a solution must resolve every subsequence on which \(K_N/N^{q_d}\to0\) and combine that answer with the established positive-lower-bound subsequences. The lower-bound branch must choose the finite-support simultaneous family \(\{\mathbf P_\theta:\theta\in\Theta_0\cup\Theta_1\}\) so that \(\Delta_{N,K}\) matches the claimed rate, \(\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{mix}}\le1/4\), and \(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{rem}}\ge0\) certifies endpoint separation against every rematching column, with strict slack away from the declared contact columns; its ordered low-versus-high version must also prove the one-sided expected-length converse. The upper-bound branch must construct a computable estimator and a uniformly honest lower bound attaining the respective rates, or prove a sharper shared-geometric dual bound if the simultaneous family cannot achieve the required separation.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The dimension-dependent estimation theorem and the plug-in honest-length theorem already settle every subsequence on which \(K_N/N^{q_d}\) is bounded below by a positive constant. The honest residual is therefore the class \(\liminf_N K_N/N^{q_d}=0\), including irregular arrays that alternate between already solved and genuinely small-ratio subsequences.

proposed.comparator_claim: On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\) balanced class, Theorem 1 gives \(N^{-1/2}+\min\{K^{-1},K^{-1/2}m^{-2/d}\}\). Their paper also covers other dimensions and \(K\ge2\); on the overlap its arbitrary-margin unit-ball model and balanced i.i.d. sampling induce this note's armwise product experiment.

Proposition 3.6 places a binary covariate-aware mirror-transport lower bound between unconditional and conditional transport, while Theorem 4.3 gives its quadratic-cost plug-in rate under smooth strongly convex Brenier potentials.
The paper proves continuity of binary conditional transport under adapted Wasserstein distance and derives a direct nonparametric estimator with a convergence rate.
The paper gives a smooth-density wavelet estimator and asymptotic normality for binary conditional transport with quadratic cost.

Theorem 22 gives the two-margin all-estimator lower bound \((m\log m)^{-2/d}\) for quadratic cost; the two-margin embedding is a subclass of the arbitrary-margin model, so its lower bound transfers upward after the displayed \(K^{-2}\) scaling, but it does not close the remaining arm factor.
Theorem 2.2 converts binary \(c\)-transform entropy into two-margin empirical transport rates.
Theorem 3.1 gives uniformly valid one-sided inference from any dual-feasible estimated pair in randomized experiments.
The paper constructs finite-sample intervals for sliced Wasserstein distance and bounds their length near the minimax rate.
The paper gives necessary and sufficient joint-mixability conditions for selected classes of univariate distributions.
Donsker dual classes yield two-margin empirical optimal-transport limits given by suprema of Gaussian processes.
Upper and lower Wasserstein dimensions determine multiscale empirical-measure approximation rates.
Quadratic negative-dependence objectives are optimized for selected identical scalar margins admitting a joint mix.
The ordered modulus gives one-sided minimax expected-length optimality for linear Gaussian regression functionals.
Optimal multi-margin dual potentials may be chosen as a simultaneously conjugate family.
Two-mode stability controls regular Monge maps for barycentric and uniformly concave sum costs.
Fixed-finite-support multi-sample optimal-transport values admit weak limits and bootstrap tests.
Sharp two-arm randomization-variance bounds yield asymptotically conservative narrow Wald intervals under unequal allocation.
Generic discrete multimarginal transport approximation has exponential tensor dependence in the number of margins.
Generic pairwise-interaction multimarginal transport is computationally hard.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Determine matching all-estimator and ordered one-sided lower bounds, or a sharper shared-geometric upper bound, on every subsequence for which \(K_N/N^{q_d}\) tends to zero, including the exact fixed-\(K\) logarithm and every transition; combine these with the already solved positive-lower-bound subsequences of each irregular legal array.
open_obligations.obstruction: The available nonparametric converse is the embedded two-margin order \(K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\), while the theoretical plug-in upper contribution is \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\). No simultaneous-marginal family has yet certified an ordered endpoint separation of the missing order while maintaining mixture total variation at most \(1/4\) and nonnegative reduced-cost slack against every rematching column, and no sharper aggregate bound for the jointly conjugate potentials is available.
open_obligations.attempted: The exact residual cap, optimal-support diameter, common-support empirical interpolation, two-margin reduction, ordered Bernoulli pair, dimension-dependent root-\(N\) results, rational certified algorithm, sparse-arm and parity examples, and fixed-dimensional orthogonal constructions have been exhausted. They settle every positive-lower-bound subsequence but do not close the small-ratio arm-factor or logarithmic gap.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For every balanced array under the maintained product experiment and unit-ball support, the already proved sandwich is
\[
c_d\max\left\{N^{-1/2},K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\right\}
\le R_d(N,K)
\le C_d\left[N^{-1/2}+\min\left\{\frac r{K^2},\frac1K m^{-2/d}\right\}\right].
\]
The already proved one-sided result is
\[
c_{d,\alpha}N^{-1/2}
\le E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)
\le C_{d,\alpha}\left[N^{-1/2}+\min\left\{\frac r{K^2},\frac1K m^{-2/d}\right\}\right].
\]
The upper length bound is attained by \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\), a theoretical uniformly calibrated rule whose constant \(C_d\) is proved to exist but is not numerically supplied. Independently, \(B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\) is fully specified, requires no transport computation, is uniformly honest, and obeys the valid baseline upper length order \(N^{-1/2}+r/K^2\). Both decision risks are of exact order \(N^{-1/2}\) on every subsequence for which \(K_N/N^{q_d}\) is bounded below by a positive constant, where \(q_5=1/6\) and \(q_d=1/4\) for \(d\ge6\). Consequently, if a legal array has \(\liminf_N K_N/N^{q_d}=0\), only its subsequences with ratio tending to zero remain unresolved; its positive-lower-bound subsequences are already settled. The rational-grid empirical multi-marginal transport algorithm separately returns primal and dual certificates with any rational requested width \(\epsilon\) in time polynomial in \(N\) and \((K/\epsilon)^d\). The missing result is a matching all-estimator and ordered one-sided converse, or a sharper aggregate upper bound, on every small-ratio subsequence, including fixed-\(K\) logarithms and every transition.

prose_updates.tldr: The target \(L(\mathbf P)\) is the sharp causal second-moment endpoint compatible with the observed arm marginals, not a centered variance endpoint. On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced arbitrary-margin class, the core sharpens Gao--Ge--Qian's empirical bound through the exact residual envelope and optimal-sum geometry. It proves matching root-\(N\) minimax estimation and uniformly honest one-sided expected excess length when \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\), where \(q_5=1/6\) and \(q_d=1/4\) for \(d\ge6\); smaller-ratio subsequences retain an arm-factor and fixed-\(K\) logarithmic gap. The fully specified mean-floor bound uses only the grand mean and needs no MOT computation. A sharper theoretical plug-in bound attains the improved length rate using a constant \(C_d\) proved to exist but not numerically supplied. The rational finite-support family is only a search template: endpoint separation, mixture indistinguishability, and resistance to every rematching column remain to be established. A separate rational-grid algorithm certifies the empirical MOT value to any requested rational tolerance. The STAR audit remains conditional on known bounded scaling and balanced subsampling and does not validate the native unequal-cell calculation.

project_justification.gap: On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced class, Gao--Ge--Qian's Theorem 1 has a \(K^{-1/2}m^{-2/d}\) term, while their printed Proposition 2 and the Manole--Niles-Weed two-margin subclass yield a \((m\log m)^{-2/d}\) converse after \(K^{-2}\) scaling. That subclass converse transfers upward to the arbitrary-margin class but leaves both a \(K\)-factor and the fixed-\(K\) logarithm unresolved. Existing work does not supply the ordered indistinguishable family needed for minimax one-sided excess length.
project_justification.niche: The squared-sum cost has shared fixed-dimensional geometry: all dual potentials obey one constraint and optimal coupling atoms permit arbitrary-subset exchanges. A successful lower family must nevertheless survive every multi-arm rematching. This makes both an aggregate dual-complexity theorem and an all-rematching simultaneous perturbation genuinely different from independent two-margin arguments.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the sharp deterministic residual and support-diameter results, a tighter empirical plug-in upper bound, and the dimension-dependent root-\(N\) elbow for estimation and honest one-sided excess length. It retains two honest procedures with different operational roles: the mean-floor rule is fully specified and uses no MOT, whereas the sharper plug-in calibration is theoretical because its finite \(C_d\) is not numerically supplied. For legal arrays with \(\liminf_N K_N/N^{q_d}=0\), the finite-support template is defined but not instantiated; matching endpoint separation, mixture indistinguishability, strict off-contact slack, and resistance to every rematching column remain explicit targets. The empirical MOT value itself has a rational primal--dual certification procedure, and the STAR audit states its additional scaling and subsampling conditions.

sampling_model.design: Balanced \(K=K_N\)-arm product experiment with \(N=Km\), fixed \(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), and \(m\to\infty\).
sampling_model.units: For arm \(k\), the observations \(X_{k1},\ldots,X_{km}\) are i.i.d. from an arbitrary marginal \(P_k\) supported on \(\mathbb B_d\), and samples are independent across arms.
sampling_model.treatment: The observed law is \(\bigotimes_{k=1}^K P_k^{\otimes m}\): it supplies one sample from each potential-outcome marginal and leaves the within-unit \(K\)-world coupling unidentified.
sampling_model.overlap: On the overlap with Gao--Ge--Qian used for comparison, both analyses have fixed \(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced allocation, arbitrary unit-ball arm marginals, and the induced armwise product law; their published scope also includes other dimensions and \(K=2\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each marginal is estimated empirically. No density, smoothness, joint-mixability, known nuisance, or centered-variance substitution is imposed. Computing \(\widehat L\) is distinct from choosing the existential constant needed to numerically report \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\); the mean-floor rule avoids both tasks.

prose_updates.related_work: Gao, Ge, and Qian define the same endpoint \(L(\mathbf P)\) and prove their displayed balanced-sample upper rate. Their published class also covers all dimensions and \(K\ge2\); every tightening claimed here is restricted to the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced class, on which both models allow arbitrary \(\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\) marginals and their balanced i.i.d. setup induces the maintained armwise product law. Their supplement localizes dual potentials coordinatewise; the present upper theorem instead uses dimension-saturated optimal-sum geometry and common-support interpolation. Manole and Niles-Weed's quadratic two-margin lower theorem applies to the embedded two-margin subclass, so its converse transfers upward to this arbitrary-margin class after the exact \(K^{-2}\) scaling, but it does not settle the missing arm factor or fixed-\(K\) logarithm. Binary covariate-aware transport, two-margin Donsker, entropy-transfer, smooth-density, sliced-Wasserstein, and regular-Monge results remain informative comparators rather than solutions to the growing-margin arbitrary-law problem. Ji, Lei, and Spector motivate dual-feasible one-sided validity but do not provide this all-arm expected-length converse. The mean-floor rule gives an independent no-MOT honest baseline; the sharper plug-in theorem is theoretical until a numerical \(C_d\) is supplied. The rational-grid theorem certifies \(L(\widehat{\mathbf P})\) itself and should not be read as computing that calibration constant. The STAR comparison is valid only after the declared affine scaling, superpopulation law, complete randomization, and randomized balanced subsampling; it does not reproduce the native \(161/37/36\) calculation.
prose_updates.interpretation: Two conclusions are settled and one is not. First, many-arm arrays at or above the dimension-dependent elbow have exact root-\(N\) estimation and honest one-sided expected-length rates. Second, users who need a fully specified bound without solving MOT can report the mean-floor rule, albeit with the coarser residual term \(r/K^2\). Third, the sharper plug-in rate is presently a theoretical existence guarantee because its calibrating \(C_d\) is not numerical. Along irregular arrays with \(\liminf_N K_N/N^{q_d}=0\), positive-lower-bound subsequences inherit the proved root-\(N\) result, while every subsequence with ratio tending to zero remains part of the frontier question.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact frontier remains open precisely on small-ratio subsequences of legal arrays with \(\liminf_N K_N/N^{q_d}=0\). The embedded two-margin converse has order \(K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\), whereas the theoretical plug-in upper theorem can retain \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\). The rational perturbation template has not yet produced endpoint separation, mixture total variation at most \(1/4\), and nonnegative reduced-cost slack against every rematching column with strict slack off contact; sparse-arm, parity, and orthogonal constructions do not bridge the gap. No aggregate localized theorem for all jointly conjugate potentials is known here either. The plug-in constant \(C_d\) is established to exist, not numerically calibrated, so \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\) is not currently a directly reportable procedure. By contrast, \(B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\) is fully specified. The fixed-dimensional rational algorithm certifies an empirical MOT value in time polynomial in \(N\) and \((K/\epsilon)^d\), not generic polynomial-time exact MOT or the plug-in confidence constant. The STAR audit discards observations and does not validate the native unequal-cell tightening.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The estimand is the uncentered second-moment endpoint \(L\). The exact residual envelope, optimal-sum diameter, improved empirical upper bound, dimension-dependent root-\(N\) estimation theorem, theoretical plug-in honest-length theorem, mean-only no-MOT baseline, rational computation certificate, hypercube parity result, and conditional STAR audit are retained. Matching estimation and expected-length rates are claimed only when \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\), with \(q_5=1/6\) and \(q_d=1/4\) for \(d\ge6\). The older \(K\gtrsim N^{1/4}\) mean-only corollaries remain valid computational baselines, not the sharp elbow. For arrays with \(\liminf_N K_N/N^{q_d}=0\), root-\(N\) is already known on each positive-lower-bound subsequence and the exact small-ratio subsequences remain open, including fixed-\(K\) logarithms and the ordered one-sided converse. The simultaneous family is a handle, not evidence that the required separation exists. The two-margin lower theorem transfers from a subclass but does not close the full-class upper gap. The plug-in confidence rule is theoretical until a computable \(C_d\) is given; the mean-floor rule is fully specified and independent of MOT. The STAR conclusions require their separately declared known bound, affine scale, superpopulation sampling, randomization, and balanced subsampling.

proofs.proof_tex:
For an observable tuple \(\mathbf P=(P_1,\ldots,P_K)\), Assumption~\texttt{ass:product-experiment} makes the observed-data law
\[
Q_{\mathbf P}=\bigotimes_{k=1}^K P_k^{\otimes m}.
\]
If \(\gamma\in\Gamma(\mathbf P)\) is an unobserved full-vector coupling, its multiworld second-moment parameter is
\[
\theta(\gamma)=\int c_K\,d\gamma
=K^{-2}\int\left\|\sum_{k=1}^Kz_k\right\|_2^2,d\gamma.
\]
Thus the identified set generated by the maintained marginal restrictions is
\[
\Theta_I(\mathbf P)=\{\theta(\gamma):\gamma\in\Gamma(\mathbf P)\},
\qquad
L(\mathbf P)=\inf\Theta_I(\mathbf P).
\]
The object estimated below is this second-moment endpoint \(L\), not the centered residual \(V\).

Define the arm and grand sample means by
\[
\widehat\mu_k=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^mX_{ki},
\qquad
\bar X=K^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^K\widehat\mu_k.
\]
By Assumption~\texttt{ass:balanced-array}, \(N=Km\), so
\[
\bar X=N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i=1}^mX_{ki}.
\tag{1}
\]
Consider the single data-driven estimator
\[
T_{\mathrm{mean}}=\|\bar X\|_2^2.
\tag{2}
\]
It depends only on the grand sample mean and does not require evaluating \(\widehat L\), solving a multi-marginal transport problem, or selecting an empirical-process constant.

We first bound its stochastic error. Since \(P_k\in\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)\), one has \(\|X_{ki}\|_2\le1\) almost surely and \(\|\mu_k\|_2\le1\). Equation~(1) and Assumption~\texttt{ass:product-experiment} imply \(\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\bar X=\bar\mu\). The centered summands from distinct pairs \((k,i)\) are independent and have mean zero. Consequently, expansion of the squared Euclidean norm gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2^2
&=N^{-2}\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i=1}^m
  \mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\|X_{ki}-\mu_k\|_2^2\\
&=N^{-2}\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i=1}^m
  \left\{\mathbb E_{P_k}\|X_{ki}\|_2^2-\|\mu_k\|_2^2\right\}\\
&\le N^{-2}\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i=1}^m1
=N^{-1}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
Both \(\bar X\) and \(\bar\mu\) belong to \(\mathbb B_d\), because each is a convex average of vectors in that ball. Hence the polarization identity, Cauchy--Schwarz, Jensen's inequality, and (3) yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}
 \left|\|\bar X\|_2^2-\|\bar\mu\|_2^2\right|
&=\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}
 \left|\langle\bar X-\bar\mu,\bar X+\bar\mu\rangle\right|\\
&\le2\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2\\
&\le2\left(\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2^2\right)^{1/2}
\le2N^{-1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]

Theorem~\texttt{thm:sharp-residual-envelope} gives, uniformly over the same arbitrary-margin class,
\[
0\le K^2\{L(\mathbf P)-\|\bar\mu\|_2^2\}=V(\mathbf P)\le r.
\]
Because \(K>0\), division by \(K^2\) is valid and therefore
\[
0\le L(\mathbf P)-\|\bar\mu\|_2^2\le\frac r{K^2}.
\tag{5}
\]
Combining (2), (4), and (5) by the triangle inequality gives the finite-sample, uniform bound
\[
\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K}
\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}|T_{\mathrm{mean}}-L(\mathbf P)|
\le2N^{-1/2}+\frac r{K^2}.
\tag{6}
\]
Taking the infimum over all measurable estimators in Definition~\texttt{def:minimax-risk} and using \(2x+y\le2(x+y)\) for \(x,y\ge0\), we obtain
\[
R_d(N,K)\le2\left(N^{-1/2}+\frac r{K^2}\right).
\tag{7}
\]

For completeness, we derive the matching all-estimator parametric lower bound rather than infer it from the displayed upper bound. Lemma~\texttt{lem:bernoulli-two-point} supplies two tuples \(\mathbf P^{(0)},\mathbf P^{(1)}\) in the model class. Write
\[
Q_j=\bigotimes_{k=1}^K(P_k^{(j)})^{\otimes m},
\qquad
\ell_j=L(\mathbf P^{(j)}),
\qquad
\Delta=\ell_1-\ell_0.
\]
That lemma states
\[
\Delta\ge aN^{-1/2}>0,
\qquad
\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\le\frac14.
\tag{8}
\]
Fix an arbitrary measurable estimator \(T\) and set
\[
D=\left\{T\ge\frac{\ell_0+\ell_1}{2}\right\}.
\]
On \(D\), \(|T-\ell_0|\ge\Delta/2\), whereas on \(D^c\), \(|T-\ell_1|\ge\Delta/2\). By the definition \(\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)=\sup_A|Q_0(A)-Q_1(A)|\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_{Q_0}|T-\ell_0|+\mathbb E_{Q_1}|T-\ell_1|
&\ge\frac\Delta2\{Q_0(D)+Q_1(D^c)\}\\
&=\frac\Delta2\{1-(Q_1(D)-Q_0(D))\}\\
&\ge\frac\Delta2\{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\}
\ge\frac{3\Delta}{8}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
At least one of the two risks in (9) is therefore at least \(3\Delta/16\). Since the supremum in Definition~\texttt{def:minimax-risk} contains both tuples and (8) holds, every estimator satisfies
\[
\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K}
\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}|T-L(\mathbf P)|
\ge\frac{3a}{16}N^{-1/2}.
\]
Taking the infimum over \(T\) proves
\[
R_d(N,K)\ge c_dN^{-1/2},
\qquad c_d:=\frac{3a}{16}>0.
\tag{10}
\]
Together, (7) and (10) prove the asserted risk sandwich, for example with \(C_d=2\); the lower constant is in fact universal and hence is admissible as a constant depending only on fixed \(d\).

Finally choose any fixed \(c_0>0\). Since \(r=\min\{K,d\}\le d\), the condition \(K\ge c_0N^{1/4}\) implies
\[
\frac r{K^2}\le\frac d{c_0^2}N^{-1/2}.
\tag{11}
\]
Substitution of (11) into (7), followed by (10), yields
\[
c_dN^{-1/2}\le R_d(N,K)
\le2\left(1+\frac d{c_0^2}\right)N^{-1/2}.
\]
These constants are uniform in \(N\), \(K\), and \(\mathbf P\). Assumption~\texttt{ass:legal-triangular-array} restricts the asymptotic assertion to balanced sequences with \(m_N=N/K_N\to\infty\); because all preceding inequalities are finite-sample, applying them eventually along any such sequence requires no interchange of limits. This proves \(R_d(N,K)\asymp N^{-1/2}\) throughout the stated large-arm regime and establishes it by the independent mean-only route.

The upper argument is a support-moment concentration argument, and the converse is an ordered two-point testing argument. Fix integers \(N,K,m\) satisfying Assumption~\texttt{ass:balanced-array}, with \(K\ge 3\) and \(m\ge 2\), and fix \(\mathbf P\in\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\). Define
\[
\varepsilon_N=(\alpha N)^{-1/2}
\quad\text{and}\quad
Y_{ki}=X_{ki}-\mu_k.
\]
Assumption~\texttt{ass:unit-ball-support} gives \(\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}Y_{ki}=0\) and
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\|Y_{ki}\|_2^2
=\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\|X_{ki}\|_2^2-\|\mu_k\|_2^2
\le 1. \tag{1}
\]
By Assumption~\texttt{ass:product-experiment}, the vectors \(Y_{ki}\) are mutually independent. Assumption~\texttt{ass:balanced-array} also implies
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\bar X
=\frac{m}{N}\sum_{k=1}^K\mu_k
=\bar\mu.
\]
Consequently the cross terms in the squared norm have expectation zero, and (1) yields
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2^2
=\frac{1}{N^2}\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i=1}^m
  \mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\|Y_{ki}\|_2^2
\le \frac{Km}{N^2}
=\frac1N. \tag{2}
\]
For the positive threshold \(\varepsilon_N^2=(\alpha N)^{-1}\), the pointwise indicator inequality
\[
\mathbf 1\{\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2>\varepsilon_N\}
\le \frac{\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2^2}{\varepsilon_N^2}
\]
and (2) give
\[
\Pr_{\mathbf P}\!\left(\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2>\varepsilon_N\right)
\le \frac{N^{-1}}{(\alpha N)^{-1}}
=\alpha. \tag{3}
\]
On the complementary event, the reverse triangle inequality gives
\[
\max\{0,\|\bar X\|_2-\varepsilon_N\}
\le \|\bar\mu\|_2.
\]
The nonnegativity assertion in Theorem~\texttt{thm:sharp-residual-envelope} is exactly
\[
L(\mathbf P)\ge \|\bar\mu\|_2^2. \tag{4}
\]
Thus Definition~\texttt{def:mean-lower-bound} and (3)--(4) imply
\[
\Pr_{\mathbf P}\!\left(B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\le L(\mathbf P)\right)
\ge 1-\alpha.
\]
Because this holds for every \(\mathbf P\in\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\), Definition~\texttt{def:honest-bounds} proves \(B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\in\mathcal H_\alpha\).

We next bound its expected excess length. Put
\[
a_\mu=\|\bar\mu\|_2,
\qquad x=\|\bar X\|_2,
\qquad b=(x-\varepsilon_N)_+.
\]
Indeed, convexity of the Euclidean ball and the triangle inequality give, almost surely,
\[
a_\mu\le \frac1K\sum_{k=1}^K\|\mu_k\|_2\le1,
\qquad
x\le \frac1N\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i=1}^m\|X_{ki}\|_2\le1,
\qquad
0\le b\le x.
\]
Thus \(0\le a_\mu,x,b\le1\). Moreover,
\[
|a_\mu-b|
\le |a_\mu-x|+|x-b|
\le \|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2+\varepsilon_N. \tag{5}
\]
The upper half of Theorem~\texttt{thm:sharp-residual-envelope} gives
\[
L(\mathbf P)\le a_\mu^2+\frac r{K^2}. \tag{6}
\]
Since \((u+v)_+\le u_++v\) whenever \(v\ge0\), and since \(a_\mu+b\le2\), equations (5)--(6) yield the pointwise inequality
\[
\begin{aligned}
\bigl(L(\mathbf P)-B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\bigr)_+
&\le \frac r{K^2}+(a_\mu^2-b^2)_+\\
&\le \frac r{K^2}+2|a_\mu-b|\\
&\le \frac r{K^2}
   +2\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2+2\varepsilon_N.
\end{aligned} \tag{7}
\]
For the nonnegative variable \(Z=\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2\), the elementary inequality \((\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}Z)^2\le\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}Z^2\), together with (2), yields \(\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2\le N^{-1/2}\). Taking expectations in (7), then taking the supremum over \(\mathbf P\), gives
\[
\sup_{\mathbf P}
\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\!\left[\bigl(L(\mathbf P)-B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\bigr)_+\right]
\le \frac r{K^2}+\bigl(2+2\alpha^{-1/2}\bigr)N^{-1/2}. \tag{8}
\]
Because \(B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\in\mathcal H_\alpha\), Definition~\texttt{def:minimax-excess-length} and (8) establish the desired upper bound with, for example, \(C_{d,\alpha}=2+2\alpha^{-1/2}\).

For the converse, invoke Lemma~\texttt{lem:bernoulli-two-point}. Let \(\mathbf P^{(0)},\mathbf P^{(1)}\) be its two tuples, write \(L_j=L(\mathbf P^{(j)})\), and let \(Q_j\) denote the corresponding law of the full sample under Assumption~\texttt{ass:product-experiment}. The lemma gives
\[
L_1-L_0\ge aN^{-1/2}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\le\frac14, \tag{9}
\]
where \(a>0\) is universal. Fix any \(B_N\in\mathcal H_\alpha\). Honesty under \(Q_0\) and the defining inequality \(Q_1(A)\ge Q_0(A)-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\) for total variation imply
\[
Q_1(B_N\le L_0)
\ge Q_0(B_N\le L_0)-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)
\ge 1-\alpha-\frac14
\ge\frac12, \tag{10}
\]
where the last inequality uses \(0<\alpha<1/4\). On \(\{B_N\le L_0\}\), equation (9) implies \((L_1-B_N)_+\ge L_1-L_0\ge aN^{-1/2}\). Hence
\[
\sup_{\mathbf P}\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}[(L(\mathbf P)-B_N)_+]
\ge \mathbb E_{Q_1}[(L_1-B_N)_+]
\ge \frac a2N^{-1/2}. \tag{11}
\]
Taking the infimum over \(B_N\in\mathcal H_\alpha\) proves the lower bound with \(c_{d,\alpha}=a/2\).

Finally, if \(K\ge c_0N^{1/4}\), then \(r=\min\{K,d\}\le d\) and
\[
\frac r{K^2}\le \frac d{c_0^2}N^{-1/2}. \tag{12}
\]
Combining (8), (11), and (12) proves \(E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\asymp N^{-1/2}\) throughout this regime; because \(c_0\) is fixed and may depend only on \(d\), the comparison constants depend only on \(d\) and \(\alpha\). Assumption~\texttt{ass:legal-triangular-array} specifies the legal asymptotic sequences along which this comparison is read. The construction is an independent mean-only baseline: its displayed formula uses only \(\bar X\), \(N\), and \(\alpha\), so its implementation neither computes an empirical transport endpoint, solves a multi-marginal optimal-transport problem, nor selects an existential empirical-process calibration constant.

proposed.statement: For constants \(0<c_{d,\alpha}\le C_{d,\alpha}<\infty\), \(c_{d,\alpha}N^{-1/2}\le E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\le C_{d,\alpha}(N^{-1/2}+r/K^2)\), and \(B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\in\mathcal H_\alpha\). Consequently \(E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\asymp N^{-1/2}\) when \(K\ge c_0N^{1/4}\).
proposed.justification: Uniform coverage and expected shortfall are treated as a decision problem distinct from point estimation.
proposed.gap: Ji--Lei--Spector prove broad dual-feasible uniform validity, and Manole--Balakrishnan--Wasserman prove near-minimax intervals for sliced Wasserstein distance; neither gives this all-arm one-sided endpoint-length converse.
proposed.consumer: A reported MOT tightening can be accompanied by a lower confidence endpoint whose worst-case conservatism is quantitatively controlled.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof directly uses unit-ball support to obtain the uniform second-moment bound for the pooled sample mean, so that assumption must be wired into the theorem rather than left implicit.
